best_for: Developers, students and data hobbyists who need to open, inspect or fix a SQLite file and would rather click through tables than type every query in the sqlite3 shell.

points.title: A spreadsheet view of your database
points.text: Browse, sort, search and edit records in a grid, and create or change tables and indexes without writing the SQL yourself. A full SQL tab is there when you want it.

points.title: Gets data in and out
points.text: It imports and exports CSV, plain text and SQL dump files, and can draw simple plots from a table or query. A log shows every SQL command the app runs for you.

points.title: Handles encrypted files
points.text: It can open SQLCipher databases and add, change or remove their encryption.

points.title: Free and local
points.text: No account and no price. The code is open source under MPL-2.0 and GPL-3.0 or later. It works on database files on disk, not on database servers, and the related DBHub.io sharing site was shut down in February 2025.

points.title: Releases are slow
points.text: The current release, 3.13.1, dates from October 2024. For bugs fixed since then, the project points to nightly builds for Windows, macOS and Linux.

points.title: Builds for every kind of PC
points.text: Windows MSI installers come in 32-bit, 64-bit and Arm64 and install for all users; zip and PortableApps versions exist too. The Mac build is a universal .dmg. On Linux, the Flatpak here is verified on Flathub, so it comes from the project.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 8 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
